quorum.judges_note: THE JUDGES ARE THE LANES. This cut ran no second-tier judge phase: the same three lanes that reviewed the diff are the panel each claim was put to, so judges=3 and refuters_per_claim=3 count the SAME three reviewers rather than two independent tiers, and PMAT-549 (two rounds of three lanes each followed by three separate judges) is the stronger shape. Recorded here so the two numbers are not read as six reviewers. The refutations in this cut came from the release gates, not from the panel — see .quorum/evidence/release-1.30.0-judges.md, which names them as the refuting authority.

falsification.test: falsification_release_changelog_counts_the_window (5 cases, all pass on this tree) is the falsifier this cut RESTS on rather than one it adds: it is the test that makes the CHANGELOG window rule refutable, and this cut is an instance of that rule. No new test is owed, because the diff changes no Rust — gate F reports no .rs differs from origin/main. The behaviour being released was falsified on its own branch: #551 carries four integration cases and eleven unit cases, with origin/main src/ checked out over the head to watch all four fail.

tool_defects_found: forjar#554 — the quorum gate hashes docs/audits/quorum-*.json, which the review tooling writes, so committing a verdict moves the hash the receipt binds and each round invalidates itself. Hit while cutting this release; the workaround here is not to commit that file, and the fix is a .gitignore entry matching the convention main already follows.
